items.title: Facebook, TikTok shut down in Equatorial Guinea
items.description: Facebook and TikTok have been inaccessible for more than two weeks in Equatorial Guinea, an AFP journalist said on Wednesday, after a video accusing the vice-president of corruption went viral. The authoritarian central African country, which has been ruled by President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo since 1979, is regularly accused of repression of civil liberties. Internet speed has been restricted since September 2 and access to Facebook and TikTok — the country’s most popular online platforms — has been impossible for anyone without a virtual private network. Other Meta platforms such as WhatsApp and Instagram, are limited but working. The apparent block on Facebook and TikTok comes after a young woman accused the president’s eldest son, Vice President Teodoro Nguema Obiang, of corruption in an online video. She was then arrested by the authorities. The vice-president — nicknamed Teodorin — is known for his luxury lifestyle that he posts on social networks. He was convicted in France in 2021 in a trial over “ill-gotten gains” and saw his assets frozen in the United Kingdom following investigations into acts of corruption. There was no immediate response from the information ministry when contacted by AFP. In Gabon, which borders Equatorial Guinea, social networks have been suspended since February, officially to combat the dissemination of “content… undermining… the stability of the institutions of the republic and national security”. AFP The post Facebook, TikTok shut down in Equatorial Guinea appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana-Russia relations must deliver more opportunities for young people – Opare Addo
items.description: Minister for Youth Development, George Opare Addo, has praised the longstanding relationship between Ghana and Russia, calling for deeper cooperation that delivers tangible opportunities for young people in both countries. He reiterated the relations between Ghana and Russia, which date back several decades, particularly to the era of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah. The Minister acknowledged that the relationship has contributed significantly to educational and human capital development for Ghana. Speaking in an interview on the sidelines of the ongoing 2026 International Festival of Youth (IFY) in Ekaterinburg, Russia, Mr Opare Addo said many Ghanaians had benefited from scholarships to study in Russia over the years. According to him, a number of those beneficiaries have since returned to Ghana and are contributing their knowledge and expertise to the country’s development in various sectors. “I know Ghana and Russia have a longstanding relationship of corporation over the years, it started from our first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah and his association in the Soviet Union then and since that time, I know Russia has provided a lot of scholarship opportunities to Ghanaian students. A lot of my colleagues had the opportunity to study here, in Russia and they are back home, working to develop our country,” he said. The Youth Development Minister expressed optimism that the longstanding friendship would continue to evolve into partnerships that provide mutual benefits for both countries. He particularly wants future cooperation to place greater emphasis on programmes and initiatives capable of transforming the lives of young people, including opportunities in education, technology, skills development, innovation and other areas of youth development. “Going into the future, technology has become a very important aspect of development, entrepreneurship has become a bedrock of our development and I believe strongly that, that level of corporation we are seeking now, “When I come into office as Youth Development Minister, I engaged the Deputy Ambassador for Russia (to Ghana) to find out on how we can corporate and develop our young people who are willing to come here and learn, we are more than wiling to come here and learn,” he noted. “We can only pray that we deepen this relationship where it becomes mutually beneficiary to both countries,” he added. He expressed hope that the relationship would continue to grow, allowing Ghana and Russia to learn from each other and pursue areas of cooperation that advance their shared interests. The Minister made the remarks while attending the 2026 International Festival of Youth in Ekaterinburg, where young people and officials from Ghana are participating alongside delegates from other countries. The festival, which runs from September 11 to 17, brings together young leaders and professionals from across the world for discussions and activities spanning education, entrepreneurship, technology, media, culture and international cooperation.

items.title: Indian delegates attempt to interrupt Ayaz Sadiq’s address at Commonwealth conference
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Indian delegates reportedly attempted to interrupt National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq’s address at the 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference in Cape Town, South Africa, as he spoke about climate adaptation and climate justice. According to information available, the Indian delegates repeatedly sought to intervene during Sadiq’s speech, with footage showing attempts to get hold of the microphone and disrupt the proceedings. Sadiq had raised the issue of “water terrorism” during his address without naming any country, in the context of broader concerns over climate change, water resources and climate justice. The Indian delegates’ attempts to seize the microphone affected the atmosphere of the session, prompting direct intervention by the host and the Jamaican speaker, who asked them either to remain silent or leave the hall. Meanwhile, other participants advised the Indian delegates to listen patiently to Speaker Sadiq’s address. Despite the disruption, the discussion on climate adaptation and climate justice continued. In his address, Speaker Sadiq, without naming any country or delegation, presented a principled position on tackling climate change and stressed the responsibilities of the international community. He raised issues, including the sudden surge of water in rivers and the withholding of water, without naming any country. Speaker Sadiq said climate adaptation policies should be formulated with effective public participation, adding that oversight by democratic institutions was indispensable to policies aimed at addressing climate change. He added that climate change was affecting various spheres of life, including food, water and health, noting that Pakistan was among the countries most affected by climate change. “Tackling climate change requires climate justice and the inclusion of democratic institutions,” he said, adding that parliamentary dialogue on global challenges such as climate change should be serious, purposeful and constructive. He said the role of parliaments was important in the practical implementation of climate policies and that international climate finance should come under parliamentary oversight. “The Parliament of Pakistan is playing an important role in climate adaptation through legislation, budgetary oversight and committees,” he said, adding that the inclusion of women, youth and other segments of society was indispensable to addressing climate change. “To deal with climate risks, parliaments should benefit from mutual experiences,” he said, adding that to meet the challenges of climate change, parliaments should promote cooperation and meaningful dialogue rather than differences. “Strong democratic institutions are indispensable for strong and vibrant societies,” Speaker Sadiq said, adding that climate adaptation could be effective only with fair financial assistance and democratic accountability. The Indus Water Treaty (IWT) remains a contentious issue between Pakistan and India, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025. Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. In August, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) in the Hague also ordered India to uphold the IWT with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir.

items.title: INEC: Amupitan away on official assignment
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained that its Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, is currently away from Abuja on an official assignment, stressing that he has the authority to delegate his responsibilities to any National Commissioner. INEC Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Mrs Victoria Eta-Messi, gave the clarification in response to questions raised by the Obidient Movement over the whereabouts of the Chairman. “The Chairman is on an official assignment outside Abuja. He can delegate powers to any National Commissioner,” Eta-Messi said in a brief message to our correspondent via WhatsApp. The clarification followed a statement by the Obidient Movement on Wednesday, in which it demanded an explanation from INEC over Amupitan’s whereabouts after National Commissioner, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, appeared as Acting Chairman during an engagement with an African Union delegation at the commission’s headquarters in Abuja. The movement, through its National Coordinator, Dr Yunusa Tanko, questioned why there had been no public announcement explaining when or why Amupitan handed over his duties to Gumus. It also asked the commission to disclose whether the Chairman had travelled outside Nigeria and, if so, provide details of his official engagements. “As far as the Obidient Movement and Nigerians are concerned, there was no official communication of Professor Amupitan’s handover to anyone, either in acting or substantive capacity. “This raises legitimate questions about the Chairman’s current location, official schedule and the circumstances surrounding his absence,” the statement partly read. Tanko said the questions were necessary because of INEC’s constitutional responsibility for conducting elections and the importance of public confidence in the commission’s leadership ahead of the 2027 general elections. “As Nigeria moves closer to the 2027 general elections, the INEC Chairman cannot operate in secrecy,” he said. However, checks by our correspondent on INEC’s official X, formerly Twitter, and Facebook accounts showed that Amupitan had been engaged in official activities outside the country. A post on Friday showed the Chairman in Ottawa, Canada, where he met with Google Global Lead, Civic Responsibility, David J. Lopez, accompanied by INEC Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Global Conference on Responsible AI and Elections. Earlier on Thursday, Amupitan held strategic partnership meetings with senior officials of Microsoft and the International Foundation for Electoral Systems. At the meeting with Microsoft officials, Ethan Chumley, Emerging Tech and Cyber Lead, and Ariana Molina, Programme Manager, discussed areas of mutual interest in emerging technologies, cybersecurity and responsible artificial intelligence, particularly their application to strengthening the resilience and security of electoral processes. Amupitan also addressed the AI conference, where he shared Nigeria’s experience and lessons in institutionalising responsible AI for electoral administration. The development comes amid heightened scrutiny of INEC as preparations intensify for the 2027 general elections. Meanwhile, another senior INEC official, who spoke with our correspondent on condition of anonymity, described the Obidient Movement’s concern as “a non-issue”, saying the Chairman was not required to be physically present at the commission’s headquarters in Abuja to perform his duties. “It is a non-issue. Must he be in Abuja to perform his duties? So, if I were to go on leave, can’t I hand over to someone until I return? “The Chairman is attending a conference and even gave an address at the conference. He had some meetings too. So what is the issue? It’s just noise,” the official said. The post INEC: Amupitan away on official assignment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Govt working to introduce virtual grid system, says power minister
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Power Minister Awais Leghari on Wednesday said the government was working to introduce a virtual grid system in the country, under which consumers would be able to generate and store electricity. Talking to the media after a National Assembly panel meeting, the minister said work on regulations for virtual grids had already started and that the regulations would be finalised by the last quarter of the current fiscal year. The minister said power distribution companies (Discos) had also been directed to install batteries on their grids as part of efforts to improve the power system and promote energy storage. “A battery revolution is coming to Pakistan as the government seeks to promote battery use and introduce a virtual grid system,” he said. “The government’s objective is to increase the use of batteries in the country’s power sector.” Earlier, the minister faced a tough time at the NA Standing Committee on Power meeting as committee chairman Muhammad Idrees questioned him about prolonged electricity load-shedding in the country. During the meeting, Leghari acknowledged that load-shedding was being carried out on around 3,500 of the country’s 14,500 feeders due to electricity theft and line losses. “Within a year, the government will shift load-shedding from feeders to transformers so that an entire feeder will not have to be shut down,” he said, adding that the government was also introducing an on-off control system for around 190,000 transformers. With the new system, he said, it would not be necessary to shut down an entire feeder, while consumers who regularly paid their electricity bills would not be affected. He said there was currently no additional load-shedding in the country. “The outages are mainly occurring due to faults caused by overloading of the power system.” Leghari said heavy investment was required to upgrade the power system and that approval from the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) would be sought for the upgrades. Regarding the energy situation, the minister said the closure of the Strait of Hormuz had affected the Petroleum Division’s ability to receive LNG cargoes. He said the government was using locally produced gas for power generation. Explaining the decision to carry out load-shedding at night, Leghari asked, “Who will bear an additional electricity bill of Rs6 to Rs6.50 per unit?” He said a gas cargo that previously cost around $30 million was now costing more than $95 million, making it necessary to take measures to reduce fuel costs. “We carried out load-shedding during peak hours to save fuel costs,” the minister said. He clarified that the government had not signed any new agreement with any independent power producer (IPP), adding that incorrect reports had appeared in the media on the matter. During the meeting, PML-N MNA Rana Muhammad Hayat said there was a lot of discussion but electricity prices had not come down. “There is so much load-shedding that it has become difficult for us to go among the people,” he said. Hayat also criticised the performance of the Discos, but ended up blaming the policymakers and the ministry for the state of affairs in the power sector. “What can the Discos do, minister sahab ? You switch off the electricity,” he said. The PML-N lawmaker said the government’s policies gave the impression that it was working primarily to meet the requirements of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), rather than addressing people’s problems. “Yes, I feel like we are working not for the country but only for the IMF,” he said. The minister, however, responded that Hayat was making an irresponsible statement at a responsible forum.

items.title: Kwadaso NDC supporters demand removal of MCE over ‘Nkoko Nkitinkiti’ project
items.description: Some supporters of the National Democratic Congress in the Kwadaso Constituency of the Ashanti Region have taken to the streets to demand the removal of the Municipal Chief Executive, Eric Asibey, over alleged poor execution of the government’s poultry project, popularly known as “Nkoko Nkitinkiti.” The protesters allege that only about 3,000 birds were distributed instead of the 10,000 allocated to the constituency. One of their placards read: “Where are our 10,000 Nkoko Nkitinkiti? You gave us only 3,000.” According to the party faithful, the shortfall undermines the government’s poverty alleviation efforts. The group, comprising ward coordinators, branch executives and supporters, also accused the MCE of corruption and failing to support development in the municipality. During the demonstration, they presented a petition to the constituency party executives listing several allegations against the MCE. Speaking to journalists, the NDC Branch Youth Organiser for Sofoline, Abdul Aziz Haruna, said the grassroots had engaged the MCE on several occasions with recommendations to improve the welfare of constituents and party supporters. “The MCE is allegedly cutting deals with car dealers at Sofoline and Kwadaso Edwenease. He is also allegedly involved in other corruption-related issues in the constituency,” he claimed. They are therefore calling on President Mahama, the Chief of Staff, the Minister for Local Government, the Ashanti Regional Minister, and the party’s national, regional and constituency executives to revoke Mr Asibey’s appointment. The MCE, Eric Asibey, has denied all the allegations, insisting his administration has discharged its mandate effectively. According to him, the Assembly distributed 3,800 birds under the Nkoko Nkitinkiti programme, which is the quantity received so far. “I have a report to prove we shared 3,800 out of the 10,000 allocations. It was communicated to us that a farmer is brooding the birds for us, and we were given the 3,800. The Agric Director has a report on that to be presented to the Ministry. We have evidence to support the quantity we had,” he said. He also refuted claims of corruption and expressed willingness to work with all factions to develop the municipality.

items.title: Ebonyi 2027: Our campaign will be issue-based — Odii
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Ebonyi State, Chief Ifeanyichukwuma Odii, has warned against violence and bloodshed before, during and after the 2027 governorship election. Odii, who spoke during the flag-off of his campaign in Abakaliki, said his campaign would be issue-based and devoid of rancour, name-calling and intimidation. He said he was contesting the election to “rescue Ebonyi State”, stressing that there would be no room for politics of hate, harassment or assault. Odii, who was represented at a press briefing to kick-start the campaign by the PDP Publicity Secretary, Mr Darlington Onwe, said the party had also commenced an empowerment programme for its members and residents of the state. He said: “As the embargo has been lifted for all campaign activities and we step into the field, let me remind us that our campaign will be strictly issues-based. We are running this election together to rescue our state; therefore, there will be no room for the politics of hate, intimidation, harassment, or any form of assault. “We will not throw a stone into a crowded market, as it may hit one of our own. However, we will never tolerate any form of state-sponsored hostility. We shall keep our eyes firmly on the ball, anchored by an absolute commitment to the rules of engagement.” Odii said no political ambition was worth the life of any citizen and urged political actors to avoid actions capable of triggering violence. “No leadership ambition is worth the life or blood of any citizen. Any leader who attacks or sponsors violence against their people simply because of their choice of party or lawful association has missed the mark and failed the test of genuine love for the people. We will not give in to any form of violence or intimidation,” he said. The PDP candidate also promised to prioritise youth development, saying his administration, if elected, would treat young people with dignity and provide opportunities for them to build sustainable livelihoods. He said his campaign would be anchored on his blueprint, titled A Promise of Possibility, which he said was designed to address poverty and promote development across key sectors. According to him, his administration would seek to transform Ebonyi into “a globally competitive, industrialised, innovation-led, and investment-ready economy” through investments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture, enterprise development and social protection. He promised to create jobs, support businesses, modernise agriculture, empower women and youths, improve healthcare and infrastructure, and strengthen security and justice across the state’s 13 local government areas. Odii promises free education On education, Odii promised free and compulsory education from primary to secondary school if elected governor. He also pledged free tertiary education for Ebonyians studying medicine, specialised science and critical technology-related courses. “In education, human capital development, and the knowledge economy, we will create a symbol of freedom by providing free and compulsory education from primary through secondary school. “Furthermore, we shall grant free tertiary education for every Ebonyian studying medicine, specialised science, and critical technology fields,” he said. Odii also promised to reform the state’s agricultural sector by moving farmers from subsistence production to what he described as a modern agribusiness-driven economy. He said his administration would establish Farmer Income Stabilisation and Social Safety-Net Schemes to protect farmers against floods, price collapses and poor farming seasons. He further promised to establish agro-processing plants and an Agro-Industrial Park for rice, cassava, yam and other priority crops to increase value addition and create jobs within the state. On healthcare, Odii pledged to expand affordable services across all 13 local government areas, with the aim of reducing the financial burden of illness on families. He also promised to leverage Ebonyi’s solid mineral resources, including limestone, crushed stone and the salt lakes in Okposi and Uburu, as well as the digital and creative economies, to expand the state’s revenue base. The PDP candidate said his administration would also introduce merit-based recruitment, transparent public financial management and performance-based governance. He disclosed that the party had resolved to empower 20 people in each ward across the state as part of its ongoing programme. According to him, the initiative would subsequently be extended to the polling-unit level, with ward leaders expected to oversee the selection of beneficiaries for the first phase. He said the state-level campaign would be followed by campaigns at the local government and ward levels. Odii also thanked party leaders, elders, women, youths and grassroots members for their support, saying their commitment was critical to the campaign. “Our greatest strength lies in the fact that our people are with us; they are eager for change, growth, progress, and prosperity. The time to make it happen is now,” he said. The post Ebonyi 2027: Our campaign will be issue-based — Odii appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Abrika CHPS compound to end maternal health nightmare for Techiman-Sunyani communities
items.description: The dusty roads linking Bridgeso and Abrika to Techiman have, for decades, borne the weight of countless tragedies. Women in active labour pleading for transport. Children slipping into critical malaria comas. The elderly gasping for oxygen. With the only health facility miles away in Techiman, these communities have endured a healthcare crisis that has cost lives and broken families. “We have lost too many mothers on this road,” lamented Nana Kwame Boakye, an opinion leader in Bridgeso, reflecting on the perennial nightmare. “Not just women in labour, but children with malaria, the elderly with high blood pressure. By the time you arrange transport to Techiman, it is often too late. We have been crying for help for years.” For expectant mothers, the situation has been particularly dire. Without a nearby health post, many have been forced to deliver at home without skilled care, or risk the perilous journey to Techiman in the final moments of labour—a gamble that has too often ended in tragedy. “When my daughter went into labour with her first child, we had to rush her to Techiman,” recounted Akua Afriyie, a resident of Bridgeso. “The road was bad, it was night, and we thought we would lose both of them. By the grace of God, they survived, but not every woman is that lucky. We have lost mothers here. We have lost babies. It breaks your heart.” Her story is echoed by Adwoa Takyiwaa, a young mother from Abrika, who lived in constant fear throughout her pregnancy. “When I was pregnant, I was terrified. I knew if I went into labour at night, I might not make it to the hospital. Some of my friends had their babies on the roadside. We prayed and prayed for a health centre to be built here. We need help. Our children deserve to be born safely.” The lack of healthcare infrastructure has not only affected maternal health but has also left the entire population vulnerable to preventable diseases and emergencies. The cries of these communities have finally been heard. The Techiman Municipal Assembly, recognising the urgent need, has initiated the construction of a modern CHPS compound designed to bring primary healthcare to the very doorsteps of these long-neglected villages. On Thursday, the Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, visited the site to assess the progress of work. Walking through the half-finished wards, inspecting the quality of the masonry, and receiving briefings from site engineers, the Minister—who has been a vocal advocate for improved primary healthcare—expressed satisfaction with the quality of work but stressed the need for urgency. “I am very impressed with the quality of work I have seen here today. The contractor is doing a commendable job. The foundations are strong, the walls are solid. This is the kind of quality we expect,” Mr Owusu Antwi stated. “However, I must urge the contractor to speed up his work. The people of Bridgeso, Abrika, and the surrounding communities need this facility urgently. Every day of delay is a day a mother or child could be at risk.” The government’s commitment to strengthening primary healthcare across the region is evident. Mr. Owusu Antwi has previously noted that construction works on 18 CHPS projects were at various stages of completion in the Bono East Region, and the government had approved the construction of additional CHPS compounds to improve healthcare delivery. CHPS compounds play a critical role in preventive healthcare, early disease detection, and the provision of maternal and child health services. The project is more than just a clinic. Municipal Engineer Kofi Oduro explained the comprehensive scope of the facility, noting that its design addresses the key challenges that have plagued rural healthcare delivery. “This is a comprehensive project. It is not just a clinic. We are constructing a fully-fledged CHPS compound with a consulting room, a delivery room, an outpatient department, and importantly, accommodation for health workers,” Engineer Oduro explained. “We have also included facilities for staff quarters because we know that without housing, it is difficult to attract and retain nurses and midwives to serve in these rural areas.” The inclusion of staff accommodation is a crucial feature. In many rural areas across the Bono East Region, the lack of housing has been a major deterrent for health workers, leaving communities without essential care. This project aims to solve that problem from the outset, ensuring that once completed, the facility will be fully staffed and operational. For the residents watching from the sidelines, the sight of the Minister and the engineers inspecting the facility is a moment of validation—a sign that their long wait may soon be over. Nana Kwaku Yeboah, an elder in the village, expressed gratitude on behalf of the community and pledged their support to protect the facility. “We are grateful to the government and the Municipal Assembly for this project. Our people have suffered for too long. When this facility is completed, it will save lives,” he said. “We promise to support and protect it. It is our facility, and we will take care of it.” With the Minister’s call to speed up work, the contractor has pledged to mobilise more resources to ensure timely delivery. The Bono East Regional Minister has emphasised that the government remains committed to strengthening healthcare delivery across underserved communities through sustained investment in CHPS compounds. For the women of Bridgeso and Abrika, the promise of a nearby delivery room is a dream that is finally taking shape. For the children, it is the hope of a healthier future. And for the entire community, it is the end of a long and dangerous journey—a journey that, very soon, they will no longer have to make.

items.title: No going back on concession — Education Minister
items.description: By Adesina Wahab, Joseph Erunke and Matthew Johnson The Federal Government on Wednesday ruled out any reversal of its decision to concession the management of King’s College, Lagos, to the institution’s Old Boys Association, as policemen took over the school premises following days of protests over the arrangement. Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said the concession was aimed at addressing longstanding infrastructure and management challenges at the college, insisting that the Federal Government would retain ownership of the institution. The minister spoke in Abuja while briefing journalists against the backdrop of the continuing protests by workers of the Federal Ministry of Education and their unions over the proposed concession and the closure of some Federal Unity Colleges. Meanwhile, policemen drawn from various formations in Lagos State took over the premises of King’s College, Onikan, on Wednesday. The development came a day after parents protesting the concession had an altercation with policemen and members of the King’s College Old Boys Association, KCOBA. As of Wednesday morning, the protesters were no longer seen around the main gate, while roads leading to the school were cordoned off by police vehicles and officers. Vehicles approaching from the Tafawa Balewa Square end and heading towards CMS Bus Stop were diverted to alternative routes. At about 11am, members of KCOBA, including its National President, Ibrahim Kassim Imam, and former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, Mr Olumide Akpata, arrived at the school for a meeting on the concession arrangement. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the KCOBA executive committee, led by Imam, assured stakeholders that the college would be run in accordance with the principles upon which Federal Unity Colleges were established. “We are saying it again that we are not going to turn the college to an elitist one. We will run it in line with the principles behind the setting up of unity colleges and their operation. “In fact, that is contained in the agreement we signed for the concession. To say we are buying it is wrong. There is no willing seller or buyer of King’s College. The Federal Government is not selling, while KCOBA is not buying,” Imam said. He said previous interventions by old boys to rehabilitate and renovate facilities at the college had been undermined by vandalism and poor maintenance. “Our agreement with the Federal Government is open for public scrutiny. We are open to scrutiny by the public and we want the government to also look into how the school has been run so far,” he said. Imam also said KCOBA would ensure that every state of the federation was represented in the college in line with the principle of federal character. He assured stakeholders that school fees would not be increased under the arrangement. On funding, Imam said even if half of the proposed N100 billion endowment fund was realised, it would be invested to generate sustainable revenue for the running of the institution. He added that many old students were prepared to contribute to the fund once the concession took effect. The Secretary of KCOBA, Etigwe Uwa, SAN, recalled his experience as a student of the college, saying the institution had provided him with an opportunity to interact with people from different parts of the country. “I cannot be part of a system that would deny people a platform to fly. King’s College gave me such a platform and I have to extend same to others, but we must first save the college from its deplorable state,” Uwa said. Chairman of the KCOBA Week Planning Committee, Sir Gbolahan Oluyomi, also spoke about his efforts to support the digitisation of teaching and learning at the college, which he said were unsuccessful. Akpata, a former NBA president, accused some individuals of allegedly misinforming the public about the concession. “It is not correct to say we are not carrying the parents and staff along. They were always part of the meetings called by the ministry and our own meetings here,” he said. Akpata said he and members of his set had wept after seeing the state of facilities at the college during a reunion visit. A Vice-President of KCOBA, Rotimi Aladesanmi, also alleged that the principle of federal character had been undermined by what he described as admission racketeering at the college. ‘Government will not sell Unity Colleges’ In Abuja, Alausa said the Federal Government had no plan to sell any of the Federal Unity Colleges. “The Federal Government is not selling any Unity College. The Federal Government, through the Federal Ministry of Education, does not have intention to sell any Unity College, and we will not sell any Unity College,” he said. He explained that the government was considering alternative approaches to improving infrastructure and management because of the funding gap facing the education sector. According to him, the infrastructure deficit in Federal Unity Colleges had accumulated over several decades and could not be addressed solely through conventional government funding. “It is only if Mr President gives us, myself and the Minister of State, two trillion naira today, it will not be enough to fix our Unity Colleges,” Alausa said. The minister said his visit to King’s College showed that while some sections of the school were clean, the overall infrastructure was old and required significant rehabilitation. He rejected the argument that concessioning the institution amounted to selling government property, stressing that ownership would remain with the Federal Government. Alausa also accused some directors in the ministry of allegedly instigating workers against the government’s policy, saying the government had intelligence identifying officials allegedly involved in mobilising staff against the concession. “It’s obvious now that some directors in the Ministry of Education are instigating their staff. We have intelligence to show us some directors in the Ministry of Education that are instigating their staff,” he said. He said the government had engaged the unions and reached a six-point agreement intended to resolve the dispute and pave the way for workers to return to their offices. He, however, said another faction of the protesting workers had failed to meet conditions set by the ministry for further engagement. Alausa said the government recognised the right of workers to protest but insisted that such protests must be conducted within the law. “To maintain peace and harmony, we will not allow people to take laws into their own hands. This is a responsible government. We have given them all the room and scope for them to do their protests within the ambit of the law. There is a limit to government patience,” he said. The minister also dismissed claims being circulated by some workers and unions over the dispute as misinformation. Meanwhile, the Federal Unity Colleges remained shut on Wednesday amid the continuing industrial dispute. Concession to run for 25 years Also speaking, the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Said Ahmad, said the Federal Government remained open to dialogue with the unions but insisted that normalcy must first return to the ministry. Ahmad said one of the major issues surrounding the resistance to the concession appeared to be opposition to change and reluctance by some stakeholders to move away from existing arrangements. She disclosed that the proposed concession of King’s College would run for 25 years. According to her, the period was considered necessary to enable the concessionaire to establish sustainable management structures and systems and allow the government to assess the effectiveness of the arrangement. The dispute over King’s College and the broader management of Federal Unity Colleges continues to generate tension between the Ministry of Education and its workers, with the unions maintaining their objections to the government’s proposed reforms. The post No going back on concession — Education Minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Renouvellement du bureau syndical de l’AN : Alphonse Charles Wright réunit les protagonistes et appelle au dialogue
items.description: À l’issue d’une médiation conduite la semaine dernière par le procureur spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), Alphonse Charles Wright, ayant permis à la section syndicale de l’Union des travailleurs parlementaires de reporter l’élection pour le renouvellement de son bureau à une date ultérieure afin de favoriser les négociations, le processus a franchi un nouvel épisode. C’est dans cette dynamique qu’une rencontre s’est tenue dans la nuit du lundi 14 septembre à Kaloum entre les représentants de la section syndicale de l’Union des travailleurs parlementaires, le secrétaire général de l’Assemblée nationale, Aboubacar Camara, et le procureur spécial près la CRIEF. Cette réunion visait à donner une nouvelle impulsion au dialogue, dans le but de parvenir à une entente consensuelle et de décrisper le climat de tension entre les différentes parties. Dans un entretien accordé à Mediaguinée, le responsable communal, Daniel Tolno, a indiqué qu’à l’issue de cette rencontre, le procureur spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières a demandé au secrétaire général « de faire une note d'information à l’endroit de la centrale syndicale de l’Union Syndicale des Travailleurs de Guinée (USTG). Parce qu'il faut le rappeler nous sommes une section syndicale relevant d'une faîtière qui est l’USTG nationale. Et comme le voudrait la procédure il va le faire et proposer une date d’élection pour le renouvellement du bureau ». Selon lui, le procureur a également recommandé que les différentes parties se retrouvent afin de convenir d’une date avant de convoquer l’ensemble des travailleurs. « Il l’a fait pour eviter de trop simixter, puisque la loi est clair là-dessus il ne revient pas au pouvoir public de s'ingérer dans le fonctionnement des organisations syndicales. Le procureur spécial lui a demandé de faire en sorte qu'il ne simixte pas dans l’organisation de ce processus électoral, psrce que la loi ne lui autorise pas. Lui tous ce qu'il peut faire c’est de proposer une date et d'informer la centrale syndicale et la centrale syndicale pourra organiser une élection, puisque c’est elle qui est venue installer le premier bureau au sein de l’Assemblée Nationale, elle lui appartient donc de venir organiser l’élection pour le renouvellement du bureau », a-t-il rappelé. Par ailleurs, le procureur spécial près la CRIEF, Alphonse Charles Wright, a remercié l’ensemble des parties pour le respect de la consigne donnée, avant de les exhorter « de ne pas accepter qu'il ait de la division au sein de l’administration publique parce que ça y va dans l’intérêt de personne, de rester soudé, de garder le contact et surtout de privilégier le dialogue dans tout ce que nous aurons à faire ». Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Renouvellement du bureau syndical de l’AN : Alphonse Charles Wright réunit les protagonistes et appelle au dialogue est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: Obidient Movement demands INEC Chairman Amupitan’s whereabouts
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Obidient Movement has demanded clarification from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on the whereabouts and official engagements of its Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, following his absence from an engagement with an African Union (AU) electoral delegation in Abuja. The movement, in a statement issued by its Media and Communications Directorate on Wednesday, raised questions after INEC identified National Commissioner, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, as Acting Chairman while receiving the AU Pre-Election and Needs Assessment Mission at the commission’s headquarters in Abuja on Tuesday. INEC had said Gumus represented Amupitan at the meeting with the AU delegation, led by former Ethiopian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Demeke Mekonnen. The mission is assessing Nigeria’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections. The Obidient Movement said it was concerned that, to its knowledge, there had been no public communication explaining when or why Amupitan handed over his responsibilities to Gumus in an acting capacity. “As far as the Obidient Movement and Nigerians are concerned, there was no official communication of Professor Amupitan’s handover to anyone, either in acting or substantive capacity. “This raises legitimate questions about the Chairman’s current location, official schedule and the circumstances surrounding his absence,” the statement said. The movement called on INEC to clarify where Amupitan currently is, when he left Abuja, the official purpose of his absence and who authorised his absence from the Commission’s headquarters. It also asked the electoral body to disclose whether the chairman had travelled outside the country and, if so, the meetings or official engagements he had undertaken since his departure. The group further asked INEC to state whether Amupitan had met or was scheduled to meet President Bola Tinubu, the national chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), or any representative of the ruling party. The questions, according to the movement, were necessary because of INEC’s constitutional responsibility for conducting elections and the importance of public confidence in the leadership of the electoral commission ahead of the 2027 general elections. “As Nigeria moves closer to the 2027 general elections, the INEC Chairman cannot operate in secrecy,” the statement said. The movement also referred to what it described as Amupitan’s “antecedents and strong affection for the APC”, urging the commission to demonstrate transparency and political neutrality. It said, “The era of the INEC Chairman having strategy meetings with the APC and the ruling party must be a thing of the past. “Nigerians do not trust this INEC Chairman or the Commission he leads, so it behoves on him and the Commission to not only be transparent and non-partisan, but to also be seen as such.” The Obidient Movement further said the electoral commission should not create room for speculation about its leadership’s activities, particularly as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 elections. “It is important to reemphasise that the electoral commission belongs to the Nigerian people. Its leadership must therefore be accountable to the public and must not leave room for speculation about secret political engagements, especially given their many past antecedents and the crisis of confidence that the Commission continues to face,” it said. The movement therefore urged INEC to publicly state Amupitan’s whereabouts and explain his official engagements. Meanwhile, during Tuesday’s AU engagement, Gumus outlined INEC’s preparations for the 2027 elections and reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to electoral integrity and neutrality. She said the Commission was preparing for an election involving a voter population approaching 100 million and a workforce exceeding 1.4 million personnel. The AU mission, scheduled for September 13 to 19, is assessing Nigeria’s electoral preparedness, including voter registration, electoral technology, logistics, funding, inclusion, transparency, security coordination and results management. INEC has also previously stated that it has no preferred candidate for the 2027 election, with Amupitan stressing that the Commission’s allegiance is to the Constitution, the Electoral Act and the will of Nigerian voters. The post 2027: Obidient Movement demands INEC Chairman Amupitan’s whereabouts appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Photos: Vice President joins planting of shea seedlings at Futa Community in Tamale
items.description: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has joined the planting of specially selected shea seedlings at a demonstration farm in the Futa Community in Tamale on Tuesday, September 15. The activity formed part of her engagement at the World Shea Expo in Tamale, where she highlighted the need for increased investment in Ghana’s shea industry. She said research into new shea varieties could create opportunities to improve productivity and develop new products from a resource that has traditionally regenerated naturally across Ghana’s shea belt. The Vice President called for stronger collaboration among universities, research institutions, farmers and industry players to advance research and innovation in the sector. She also stressed the need to ensure that women, who play a central role in the shea industry, receive a greater share of the value generated along the value chain. According to her, women need better access to finance, technology and markets, as well as opportunities to establish and own businesses across the sector. She said the Women’s Development Bank could help address some of the financing challenges by providing accessible and appropriate funding to women seeking to expand their businesses. The Vice President further said investment in research, financing and processing could help make Ghana’s shea belt a stronger centre for processing, innovation and commerce. She added that such investment should ultimately ensure that more of the value generated from shea remains in the communities where the resource originates. See more photos below:

items.title: Police interdict seven officers over alleged extortion in Accra
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has interdicted seven police personnel over an alleged extortion incident in Accra involving a member of the public. According to a press statement issued on Wwednesday, September 16, the officers, who were members of a patrol team, are alleged to have demanded money from the victim and compelled him to withdraw the funds from an ATM for them. The personnel interdicted are Inspector Courage Boateng, General Sergeant Stephen Addo, General Corporal Moses Anyarvi, General Corporal Prosper Adiabo, General Lance Corporal Samuel Anokye, General Constable Henrietta Coleman and General Constable Bernard Amoako. The Police Service said the interdiction has been ordered to allow the Police Professional Standards Bureau (PPSB) to investigate the allegations. It said the matter would be thoroughly investigated and that appropriate action would be taken based on the findings of the investigation. The interdiction does not in itself establish the allegations against the officers, with the case remaining subject to the ongoing investigation by the PPSB.

items.title: NIMC, one of Tinubu’s clearest delivery stories – Akume
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, has described the National Identity Management Commission NIMC as one of the clearest delivery stories of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, citing rising enrolment and deepening integration with banking, telecommunications and social protection systems. Special Adviser to the SGF on Media and Publicity, Yomi Odunuga, said Akume made the remark on Wednesday in Abuja at the National Day of Identity 2026, themed “Nigeria’s Digital Public Ecosystem: Powering Africa’s Digital Economy”. “As the officer charged with coordinating government business across Ministries, Departments and Agencies MDAs, I have watched this work closely. The National Identity Management Commission is one of this administration’s clearest delivery stories. “The progress is real. Enrolment continues to rise. Integration with banking, telecommunications and social protection is deepening. The Commission is meeting the quiet, daily discipline this work requires. That is the kind of delivery this administration was elected to provide,” he added. The SGF said Nigeria’s expanding digital identity infrastructure was strengthening the country’s position in Africa’s digital economy, providing a trusted foundation for banking, telecommunications, social protection and cross-border trade, with implications reaching beyond the country’s borders as trusted identity infrastructure could facilitate greater economic integration across the continent. He noted that banks, fintech companies and cross-border traders increasingly rely on verified digital identity to facilitate access to markets, including opportunities created by the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Akume said the enactment of the National Identity Management Commission Act, 2026, had provided a stronger legal foundation for the country’s identity management system, strengthened data protection and established NIMC as Nigeria’s root certification authority for identity, adding that innovations introduced before the new law, including NINAuth and self-service data modification, had already made it easier for Nigerians to verify their identities and manage their records. He recalled his engagement with the Director General of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, following the passage of the Act, saying the interaction reinforced his confidence in the direction of the Commission and the seriousness of its leadership and team. “This Commission has my backing, and the backing of the office I represent. Wherever closer coordination is needed, and wherever obstacles must be cleared from this Commission’s path, my office stands ready. This project is too important to rest on one agency. It requires the full weight of government,” the SGF said. He commended President Tinubu for assenting to the NIMC Act, 2026, describing the legislation as the modern legal footing required to sustain the reforms and deepen the country’s digital identity architecture. Abuse expressed confidence that the reforms would continue to produce measurable results, saying every improvement in Nigeria’s identity infrastructure strengthens the country’s position and Africa’s participation in the global digital economy. The post NIMC, one of Tinubu’s clearest delivery stories – Akume appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GNPC sees potential 1bn barrels of oil, 2.5trn cubic feet of gas in Tano Basin
items.description: The Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) says it has identified potential stranded resources of more than one billion barrels of oil and 2.5 trillion cubic feet of gas in the Tano Basin. The Corporation says the resources could help boost Ghana’s declining petroleum production if existing infrastructure is leveraged to develop them commercially. Senior Geomatic Engineer at GNPC, Emmanuel Boadum Donkor, said spatial data analysis using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) was helping the Corporation identify ways to connect stranded resources to existing petroleum infrastructure and reduce development costs. Speaking on the sidelines of the Esri User Conference West Africa 2026, hosted by Sambus Geospatial Limited, Mr Donkor said the analysis had so far focused on the Tano Basin. “With only the Tano Basin that we have done the analysis around, we have been able to identify over 1 billion barrels of oil that we can actually potentially add to our production rate and about 2.5 trillion cubic feet of gas that we can actually add to our current production to boost it,” he said in a Citi FM interview. Hub approach to reduce development costs Mr Donkor explained that developing the stranded resources as separate projects could require significant capital investment. He said a hub-based approach, in which several resources are connected to existing infrastructure, could lower development costs and improve their commercial viability. “If you take up the CAPEX in terms of developing the infrastructure to extract these stranded resources independently, if you compare it to doing it in the hub way which we are seeking to do, you realise that it brings down the cost of investment and then it actually boosts our confidence to be able to extract these stranded resources,” he said. The approach would allow GNPC to leverage infrastructure already in place rather than developing separate facilities for individual stranded resources. GIS supporting petroleum planning Mr Donkor said GIS had become an important decision-support tool for GNPC, particularly because a significant proportion of the Corporation’s data was location-based. “At GNPC it is a very significant part of us, as our data contains about 80% location information, and that tells you how significant positioning is to our industry,” he said. He explained that GIS could combine information on wells, pipelines, roads, settlements, farms and environmentally sensitive areas to support decisions on petroleum infrastructure development while helping to minimise potential environmental and social impacts. According to him, the technology therefore provides GNPC with a clearer picture of how existing infrastructure can be integrated with stranded resources. Implementation Mr Donkor said the next phase would depend on reaching agreement on how the identified opportunities could be developed. He stressed that the resources identified through the analysis represented potential additions to production and would require the necessary investment and development arrangements before they could contribute to Ghana’s petroleum output.

items.title: JAMB moves to overhaul UTME with life skills
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, has begun a major review of the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination, UTME, with plans to introduce life skills and critical thinking into the nation’s tertiary admission test. The proposed reform could change how candidates seeking admission into universities, polytechnics and colleges of education are assessed, with greater emphasis on their ability to think, reason and apply knowledge to real-life situations. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja while inaugurating a committee of education stakeholders and experts mandated to develop a framework for integrating life skills and critical thinking into the UTME. Aina said the review had become necessary because UTME was primarily designed to rank candidates who had obtained their O-Level qualifications and should, therefore, avoid merely repeating the subject-based assessments conducted by examination bodies such as the West African Examinations Council, WAEC, and the National Examinations Council, NECO. He said candidates had already demonstrated their subject knowledge through their secondary school examinations, making it necessary for JAMB to examine whether the UTME could better assess the skills required for success in tertiary education. “So ours is a ranking task. It’s not necessarily to test your subject matter expertise. So we feel for the UTME examination to be purely subject matter is a duplicity of effort of sorts,” Aina said. The registrar challenged the committee to determine whether the existing UTME methodology was still capable of accurately predicting candidates’ prospects of success at the tertiary level. “Are the methods that we are employing to check and predict who will do well in the university or the polytechnic or the college of education, are they still valid? Are they good enough?” he asked. Aina noted that the basic UTME format had remained largely unchanged for more than three decades, stressing that changing demands in the education system made periodic review necessary. “The biggest room in the house is the room for improvement. So we want the committee to help us take a look at this,” he said. He said JAMB deliberately assembled experts and representatives from across the education sector to ensure that the proposed reform reflected broad stakeholder input. “We cannot be judges in our own matter. So we have assembled a team of stakeholders who are also experts in their own rights to join us in taking a look at this issue, to guide us and to make sure that any decision we take is one that is broadly acceptable to all the stakeholders who will be affected by these decisions,” Aina said. The committee has been given an initial four weeks to examine the proposal from a conceptual perspective, although the registrar said its tenure could be extended where necessary. “We will respond to the requests of the committee as they see fit, within reason. But they’ve been given an initial time of four weeks to look into this,” he said. Alausa seeks fair, transparent assessment The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, represented by his Technical Assistant to the Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, Mr Oni Adedeji, said the proposed reform was in line with the Federal Government’s broader efforts to transform assessment across the education system. Alausa charged the committee to develop assessment modalities that would be standardised, fair and transparent while measuring candidates’ analytical, logical and verbal reasoning abilities beyond the recall of subject content. He said the committee would also determine whether life skills and critical thinking should be assessed through a separate standardised examination or incorporated into the existing UTME subjects. The minister said the objective was to create an assessment system capable of determining not only what candidates knew but how effectively they could apply knowledge, reason and solve problems. “I strongly believe getting these rights will shape how Nigeria evaluates readiness for tertiary education now and in years to come,” Alausa said. He assured the committee of the ministry’s support and collaboration throughout the exercise. Committee seeks evidence-based reform Chairman of the committee, Prof. Boniface Nworgu of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, said the effectiveness of UTME should ultimately be assessed by its ability to identify candidates with strong prospects of succeeding in tertiary education. Nworgu explained that JAMB conducts a selection examination rather than a certificate examination, meaning that the assessment should provide reliable information on candidates’ potential to cope with academic demands at the tertiary level. “What JAMB is expected to do and what it is doing is to look at those measures that can help us to select the candidates that have the highest promise of succeeding in academic tasks at the tertiary education level,” he said. He said the validity of UTME needed continuous review because tertiary education curricula and the skills required of students had changed considerably over the years. According to him, the shift from the Benchmark Minimum Academic Standards, BMAS, to the Core Curriculum and Minimum Academic Standards, CCMAS, has placed greater emphasis on skills acquisition and critical thinking. “The focus now is the area of skills and then critical thinking. So, what JAMB is trying to do is understandable from that perspective,” Nworgu said. The committee chairman, however, said its work would not necessarily be restricted to life skills and critical thinking if its deliberations established that other measures could improve the predictive validity of UTME. “If in the course of our deliberations, we find out that there are other measures that can improve the predictive validity of the UTME, we’re certainly going to make appropriate recommendations,” he said. Nworgu said the committee would rely on evidence in assessing any proposed changes, insisting that reforms should be measurable and their outcomes capable of being evaluated. “We are not going to make that mistake in this case,” he said, referring to interventions introduced without establishing a baseline against which their effectiveness could subsequently be measured. “If we have been using UTME for this number of years and we want to produce a modified UTME, so to speak, there must be evidence at the end of the day that this effort was on time, that we did not waste the taxpayers’ money doing what is beneficial to the society,” he added. He assured JAMB that the committee would approach the assignment with the objective of producing recommendations capable of strengthening the examination. The committee comprises representatives from universities, examination bodies, professional regulatory councils, students’ organisations, secondary schools and development agencies. Members include Prof. Boniface Nworgu, chairman; Prof. M. Yakasai of Bayero University, Kano; Afolabi S. Imoukhuedе; Prof. Idris Mohammed of the Medical and Dental Council; Zakariyau Abdullahi of WAEC; Engr. Prof. Aaron Aboshio of the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria; Dr. Murtala Aliyu Sakwa of the National Board for Technical Education; Prof. Duke Okoro of the Council of Heads of Polytechnics and Colleges of Technology in Nigeria; and Jiya Umar Mohammed of the All Nigerian Conference of Principals of Secondary Schools. Others are Dr. Chima Egbujuo of the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council; Dr. Emmanuel Udontre of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria; Salawudeen Kamorudeen Opeyemi, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Students’ Engagement; Catherine-Onyejeche Ibrahim of the United Nations Development Programme; Dr. Fadipe E. Oladotun of the Veterinary Council of Nigeria; Dr. Alimigbe Frances of the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria; Lawrence B. Aremu of the National Commission for Colleges of Education; and Edidiong Lawrence Moses of the Committee of Vice-Chancellors of Nigeria. The remaining members are Prof. Raymond Emmanuel of the National Business and Technical Examinations Board; Dr. Clinton of the Nigerian Union of Teachers; Dr. Anthony Idoko of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria; Akinteye Babatunde Afeez of the National Association of Nigerian Students; Dr. Esa Onoja of the Council of Legal Education; Dr. Esther Mmekа of the National Universities Commission; Dr. Yusuf Abbas Raji of the National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies; Prof. Babawale T. Bello of the University of Lagos; and Arc. Kayode of the Architects Registration Council of Nigeria. The committee is expected to submit its initial recommendations within four weeks. JAMB will consider the recommendations before proceeding, where appropriate, to a further stage involving assessment experts who would develop and implement the details of any framework eventually adopted. The post JAMB moves to overhaul UTME with life skills appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gaza apartment block collapse leaves 21 dead
items.description: Gaza authorities said Wednesday that 21 people including five children had died after an apartment building collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes. items.title: Choix de filière universitaire au Mali, comment bien s’orienter après le bac !
items.description: Apres le baccalaureat, choisir une filiere universitaire represente un veritable defi pour de nombreux nouveaux bacheliers au Mali. Manque d'informations, pression familiale, contraintes financieres ou incertitudes sur les debouches professionnels, les obstacles sont nombreux. a quelques semaines de la rentree universitaire, comment faire un choix en adequation avec ses capacites, ses aspirations et son projet professionnel ? Pour de nombreux nouveaux bacheliers, le choix d'une filiere ne depend pas uniquement de leurs propres aspirations. L'avis des parents et de l'entourage peut egalement peser lourd dans la decision. Bacheliere, Fatoumata Cissouma explique avoir dû discuter longuement avec son pere, qui souhaitait la voir s'orienter vers la comptabilite et les finances. « Mon pere m'a conseille la comptabilite et les finances. Mais je lui ai dit que je veux etre une entrepreneuse. Parce que je vais faire gestion d'entreprise. Apres de longues discussions, il m'a dit que si j'ai des problemes, il ne va pas intervenir. Je lui ai dit que je vais assumer. » Le manque d'informations complique le choix Au-dela de la pression familiale, certains bacheliers disent manquer d'informations sur les differentes filieres et leurs debouches. Une situation qui peut alimenter la peur de faire un mauvais choix. Aly K. Diallo raconte ainsi avoir longtemps hesite avant de se decider. Il souhaitait trouver une formation correspondant a ses capacites et a son projet professionnel, mais craignait de se tromper. Cette hesitation illustre les difficultes auxquelles sont confrontes de nombreux nouveaux bacheliers au moment de choisir leur orientation universitaire. Les risques d'un choix dicte par les tendances Pour Aliou Traore, consultant en orientation et en gestion de carriere academique, le choix d'une filiere doit etre mûrement reflechi. Selon lui, une mauvaise orientation peut avoir des consequences importantes sur le parcours universitaire et professionnel. « Tous les nouveaux bacheliers maliens risquent de perdre trois ans s'ils choisissent mal leur filiere. Et egalement, le choix de leur universite joue un impact sur leur developpement de carriere. » Le consultant invite ainsi les futurs etudiants a ne pas choisir uniquement une filiere parce qu'elle est populaire ou parce qu'elle est recommandee par leur entourage. Le Salon de la rentree universitaire comme espace d'orientation Pour aider les nouveaux bacheliers a mieux s'informer, le Salon de la rentree universitaire se tient chaque annee a Bamako. L'evenement constitue un espace d'information et d'orientation destine notamment aux futurs etudiants. Il permet aux bacheliers de decouvrir differentes offres de formation, d'echanger avec des professionnels et de recueillir des informations avant de prendre une decision. L’article Choix de filière universitaire au Mali, comment bien s’orienter après le bac ! est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Deputy GMA boss denies alleged links with land guards
items.description: The Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA), Mubarick Masawudu, has denied any links to the alleged use of land guards in a land dispute at Spintex. Through his solicitors, LIMO@LAW, Mr Masawudu said he is “not a party to, nor in any way connected with,” the dispute and has never instructed, funded, or participated in any land-guard activity related to the matter. The lawyers were responding to viral reports under the headline “Maritime Authority Deputy Director Accused Of Using Land Guards In Spintex Land Dispute.” According to the lawyers, the publication was false and had subjected their client to what they described as “public opprobrium, ridicule, and hostility.” Demand to Retract and Apologise – The Insight Download They categorically stated that Mr Masawudu “is not a party to, nor in any way connected with,” the land dispute referenced in the reports. “It is a fundamental requirement of established journalistic standards that, before publication, you undertake the necessary enquiries, appropriately verify all allegations, cross-check and confirm facts,” the firm wrote, describing the paper’s conduct as “a serious departure from these sacred standards,” the statement read in parts. The solicitors are therefore demanding an unequivocal retraction and apology with the same prominence as the original publication within seven days, warning that failure to comply within the stipulated period would result in legal action “without further notice.”

items.title: Assemblée nationale : la dissolution voulue par Macron a «contribué à quasiment flinguer l’économie française», estime Attal
items.description: « Tout est parti en live, entre guillemets, avec cette dissolution qui a contribue a quasiment flinguer l'economie francaise », a affirme, ce 16 septembre, le depute des Hauts-de-Seine Gabriel Attal lors d'une intervention au « French Digital Day », evenement consacre aux startups organise a Paris, en evoquant la dissolution de l'Assemblee nationale decidee en 2024. « Avant, a l'epoque ou je suis Premier ministre, les taux [d'emprunt de la France, NDLR] etaient en moyenne entre 1,2 % et 1,5 %. Aujourd'hui, on est a 4,5 % », a affirme le secretaire general de Renaissance et candidat du parti a l'election presidentielle, sans jamais nommer Emmanuel Macron a qui il doit son ascension politique. « Avant la dissolution, on arrivait a tutoyer les 2 % de croissance. Aujourd'hui, on est quasiment en croissance nulle […] Malheureusement, la dissolution a entraîne une grande instabilite politique et donc economique », a encore affirme celui qui avait appele, lors des legislatives anticipees provoquees par cette dissolution, a « faire barrage » au Rassemblement national, y compris en votant pour un candidat de La France insoumise. « Non », lui a retorque sur X eric Ciotti, maire de Nice et president de l'Union des droites pour la Republique (UDR), avant d'ajouter : « Ce qui a "flingue l'economie", c'est votre appel a voter LFI et votre alliance de la honte avec le parti de Jean-Luc Melenchon. » Le 9 juin 2024 au soir, dans la foulee de l'annonce de la victoire du Rassemblement national aux elections europeennes, Emmanuel Macron avait prononce , a la surprise generale, la dissolution de l'Assemblee nationale. Une decision dont le chef d'etat francais se serait par la suite felicite, confiant etre « ravi » , et qui avait ouvert la voie a une crise politique inedite dans l'histoire de la Ve Republique, faute de majorite claire pour un des courants politiques representes dans l'hemicycle du Palais Bourbon.

items.title: El Gobierno escenifica avances en los Presupuestos sin fecha de presentación a la vista
items.description: A dos semanas de que expire el plazo constitucional para registrar los Presupuestos Generales del Estado en el Congreso, el Gobierno aún no ha puesto sobre la mesa una fecha para presentarlos ni tiene los apoyos políticos atados para su convalidación. Pese a ello, asegura que aprobará el proyecto antes de que termine el ejercicio y este miércoles ha escenificado avances en esta dirección: los ministros de Hacienda, Arcadi España, y de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun, han mantenido una reunión de trabajo para abordar la aprobación de las cuentas del próximo año. Serían, si prosperasen, las primeras en ver la luz desde 2023, cuando se adoptaron los Presupuestos que siguen hoy en vigor y que se han convertido, después de tres prórrogas consecutivas, en los más longevos de la democracia. items.title: South Africa’s president Ramaphosa falls ill after BRICS summit
items.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has withdrawn from public engagements after returning from the BRICS summit in India, his office said on Wednesday, citing ill health. His absence comes as Deputy President Paul Mashatile continues to recover from a minor medical procedure, leaving both of the country’s top leaders away from public duties. Ramaphosa, 73, returned from the BRICS summit in India on Monday and had been advised by his doctors to rest and recover, the presidency said. Leaders of the BRICS bloc, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, concluded a two-day summit in New Delhi on Sunday, where discussions focused on inclusive global growth and the Middle East. “Where possible, the president has asked the respective ministers to represent him at scheduled engagements,” his office said in a statement. Mashatile said on Tuesday that his “recovery is progressing well” and that he was “regaining strength each day”. “On the advice of my doctors, I will continue resting until advised otherwise while work and delegated responsibilities continue to be underway in the capable team in my office with other stakeholders in government, business and other sectors,” Mashatile said. The simultaneous absence of Ramaphosa and Mashatile comes as South Africa enters an increasingly busy political season ahead of local government elections on November 4. AFP The post South Africa’s president Ramaphosa falls ill after BRICS summit appeared first on Vanguard News .
